question: Can I release a non-native aquatic species into a lake frequented by fish in Canada?
generated_answer:
Releasing non-native aquatic species into Canadian waters is generally prohibited by law. The Fisheries Act and the Species at Risk Act protect native species and their habitats. Introducing non-native species can disrupt the ecosystem, outcompete native species, and potentially cause harm to the environment and human health. It is important to consult with local authorities or experts before releasing any species into a lake or other water body. 

If you have a non-native species that you no longer wish to keep, it is recommended to contact local pet stores, aquariums, or wildlife rehabilitation centers to find a responsible and legal way to rehome the species. 

For more information, you can refer to the following resources:

- Fisheries and Oceans Canada: [https://www.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/science/aah-saa/non-native-eng.html](https://www.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/science/aah-saa/non-native-eng.html)
- Environment and Climate Change Canada: [https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/protected-species/law-acts/non-native-species.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/protected-species/law-acts/non-native-species.html) 

Please note that the information provided here is general in nature and may not cover all specific circumstances. It is always best to consult with local authorities or experts for advice tailored to your situation.
